small_guidance:
- The kernel does only post-conv work; with fast_p=0.47 the ConvTranspose3d dominates. Tuning the fused pool/mean kernel further (BLOCK sweeps, num_warps 2/4/8) will not close the gap — at best a few % gain.
- If staying small: add `triton.autotune` over BLOCK ∈ {256, 512, 1024} × num_warps ∈ {2, 4, 8}, and consider one program per (N, C) with PK fully unrolled — current pool_total is small (8·16·16=2048) so BLOCK=2048 single-pass with num_warps=8 likely beats the loop.
- Fold the `* scale` into `inv_count` (already effectively constant) and drop the separate multiply; minor but free.
large_guidance:
- Replace the `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile) computing the input×kernel outer product and atomically scattering into the output grid, handling stride=2 / padding=1 in index math. This is the dominant op (~10ms of the 19.3ms) and the only path to meaningful speedup.
- Fuse the scale, maxpool, global-avg, and clamp into the convtranspose epilogue: since the final output is (N, C, 1,1,1), accumulate per-(N,C) max-pool windows directly as the convtranspose writes — or do a two-pass design where pass 1 is convtranspose→scratch and pass 2 is the existing fused reducer (already implemented). Prefer the latter for simplicity; the conv kernel is the bottleneck.
- Use channels_last_3d layout for the convtranspose output buffer so the (N,C) reduction in pass 2 has coalesced channel reads, and tile the scatter kernel with BLOCK_OC=16 (matches out_channels) to keep the kernel-weight broadcast in registers.
